data.name: Ankitha
data.gender_notes: Ankitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ankitha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ankita', which means 'unique' or 'unconventional'. In Hindu mythology, Ankitha is a name given to Goddess Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva. She is known for her unique beauty and intelligence, and is often depicted holding a lotus flower in her hand. The name Ankitha carries the meaning “Unique, Unconventional” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ankitha usually hope their child will grow to embody unique, unconventional and live with faith, good character and purpose.
